title: Eval: Quality Monitoring Demo with Orchard Health
summary: Redwood demo focused on Eval / Quality Monitoring: prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons. Customer (Orchard Health) is evaluating monitoring tooling to detect model drift and quality regressions across deployments (hosted vs dedicated). Key asks: easy-to-run A/B comparisons, prompt set management, privacy / SOC2 details, and pricing for a 3-week pilot.

header: Date: 2026-01-18 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom
transcript: 00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today. Quick intro - I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team, and Raj is our solutions engineer. We'll walk through Eval / Quality Monitoring: prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons. 00:15 Tom (Orchard): Hey Maya, thanks. We're primarily concerned about silent regressions when we change models; need to detect drops in clinical intent accuracy quickly. 00:30 Raj (SE): totally, that's the common ask. We'll show how prompt sets map to tests in the Console, how alerts trigger, and how you can run A/B comparisons across model variants. 00:45 Sarah (Product): quick note - privacy is big for us. We need assurance that patient PHI doesn't leave our VPC; curious about private deployment options. 01:00 Maya: absolutely. We support hosted for fast evals and Private (VPC/on-prem) for PHI-sensitive workloads. For the pilot we can run initial evals on hosted with redacted data or synthetic prompts, and then move to dedicated/private for live PII. 01:20 Raj: jumping into the Console now - here's the Eval tab, you create a prompt set: free-form text, expected label, quality rubric. You can upload CSVs or use our API. 01:35 Raj: (screen) example prompt set for triage intents: 'prescription refill', 'symptom check', etc. Each row has prompt, expected intent, notes. 01:50 Sarah: are rubrics per-prompt or per-suite? 02:00 Raj: both - you can set per-prompt tolerances and global thresholds. Alerts are evaluated against moving windows, and we do configurable smoothing to avoid noise. 02:20 Tom: what's the detection latency? If a model degrades, how quickly would we see an alert? 02:30 Raj: depends on sample volume; for our high-traffic customers alerts can trigger within minutes if you stream evals. For batch, you can schedule hourly or daily runs. 02:45 Maya: important tradeoff - more frequent checks increase cost but reduce time-to-detect. Redwood Optimize suggests sampling and batching parameters to balance cost/latency. 03:05 Priya (Platform): about A/B - can we run live A/B on production traffic with Redwood routing? 03:15 Raj: yes, smart routing supports canary and A/B with traffic splits. You can route X% to new model and compare metrics in the Console side-by-side, including custom rubrics. 03:30 Sarah: will the Console compute per-intent precision/recall or just aggregate score? 03:40 Raj: both. We compute aggregated quality scores and per-intent metrics; everything is filterable by prompt-set, model-version, and time-range. 03:55 Tom: regression alerts - do they support multi-metric triggers? e.g., drop in precision + latency spikes? 04:05 Raj: multi-metric alerting is supported; you can AND/OR conditions, and tie to alert channels (Slack, PagerDuty) or webhooks. 04:15 Maya: and for audits, we retain eval results and snapshots; in Private we can set retention policies to meet compliance. 04:30 Priya: KMS - do you integrate with customer-managed keys? 04:40 Lina (CSM): yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated; for hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit plus BYOK options for enterprise tiers. 04:55 Sarah: how noisy are the regression alerts? We don't want pager fatigue. 05:05 Raj: you can tune thresholds and use anomaly scoring. We also provide automatic suggestion for threshold based on historical variance - that's part of Redwood Optimize. 05:25 Tom: show us an A/B comparison demo - like current prod vs quantized variant. 05:35 Raj: switching screens - here's an A/B run we did: left panel shows prompt-set filters, middle shows per-intent confusion matrix, right shows time-series of delta in aggregate score. 05:50 Raj: note the 'diff view' highlights where the new model improved hallucination rate on 'medication interactions' prompts but regressed on 'follow-up scheduling' wording. 06:10 Sarah: that's exactly what we need - understanding granular regressions. 06:20 Tom: can we attach tags to prompts like 'sensitive' so they get treated differently? 06:30 Raj: yes, tag and policy rules let you mark prompts, route them for redaction, or exclude from certain evals. 06:45 Maya: regarding API - you can push eval data via our streaming eval endpoint (same auth as inference). We also have a bulk API for uploading large prompt-sets. 06:55 Priya: curious about eval compute costs - if we run nightly A/B with 50k prompts, what's ballpark? 07:10 Maya: pricing depends on token counts and model choice; we'll send sample pilot pricing. For evals we often recommend synthetic sampling and delta tests to reduce tokens. 07:30 Tom: security checklist - SOC2, SSO, audit logs. 07:40 Lina: we are SOC2 Type II; we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs in Console, and per-route access controls. We'll share the security pack after this call. 07:55 Sarah: can we automate regression remediation? e.g., rollback to previous model automatically if score drops below X? 08:05 Raj: yes - rollbacks/fallbacks are policy-driven; you can configure auto-fallback to baseline model or to a cheaper model when latency or quality thresholds are violated. 08:25 Tom: what's the onboarding time for a pilot? 08:35 Maya: typical pilot is 1-2 weeks to onboard prompt sets + run baseline tests, then 2-3 weeks of monitoring; for Private it adds infra setup. 08:50 Priya: network wise, for Private do we need to open any inbound access? 09:00 Lina: we do an outbound-only control plane option; if fully air-gapped you'd run the on-prem package. We'll include deployment notes. 09:15 Tom: any case studies in health? 09:25 Maya: we have a couple - anonymized health customers that use evals to catch hallucination regressions before rolling models. We'll send references. 09:40 Sarah: next steps - Redwood sends pricing, security docs; Orchard shares prompt sets & success metrics; schedule kickoff. 09:55 Maya: recap: send pilot SOW and security pack, Raj sends sample prompt CSV and runbook, Orchard shares prompt sets. Thanks all. 10:10 Tom: thanks, that was helpful. 10:20 Maya: we'll follow up by end of day with the docs. end
